\section{Experiments}
\label{sec:experiments}

\subsection{Setup}
\label{sec:exp-setup}

We evaluate SICA against Self-Consistency (SC) across six models, three reasoning domains, and over 3,000 condition-evaluations (${\sim}$1,250 unique instances), with diagnostic analyses of confirmation bias and process-level independence (\S\ref{sec:analysis}).

\paragraph{Models.} Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen3-14B (non-thinking mode)~\citep{yang2024qwen25}, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3~\citep{jiang2023mistral}, LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct~\citep{dubey2024llama3}, and QwQ-32B~\citep{qwen2024qwq} (7B--32B). We additionally evaluate SCB universality via cross-model extraction on five frontier models (gpt-4o, gpt-4.1, gpt-5.5, o3, Gemini-2.5-Pro; Table~\ref{tab:frontier-scb}), where Mistral-7B extracts constraints from the target model's traces since closed-source APIs do not expose internals suitable for self-extraction.

\paragraph{Datasets.} FOLIO~\citep{han2022folio} ($n{=}204$, with gold logical annotations), ProofWriter depth-5~\citep{tafjord2021proofwriter} ($n{=}600$), LogiQA~\citep{liu2020logiqa} ($n{=}200$). StrategyQA~\citep{geva2021strategyqa} ($n{=}200$) serves as a domain-formalizability diagnostic. GSM8K~\citep{cobbe2021gsm8k} (exploratory, $n{=}30$) and AIME 2024 ($n{=}22$) probe the degenerate regime ($C_0 < 5\%$).

\paragraph{Parameters.} $K{=}12$ traces at $T{=}0.7$, extraction at $T_{\text{ext}}{=}0.3$, $\alpha{=}0.5$, Z3 timeout 10s. McNemar exact test ($\alpha{=}0.05$); 95\% bootstrap CIs ($10{,}000$ resamples) for $n \geq 200$. SICA incurs $4.5{\times}$ SC wall-clock; extraction accounts for 76\% of overhead.


\subsection{Main Results}
\label{sec:main-results}

Table~\ref{tab:main_results} reports accuracy across all conditions sorted by SC baseline, revealing three observation-driven accuracy regimes.

\begin{table*}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{SICA vs.\ SC across all non-degenerate self-extraction conditions (sorted by SC). No condition shows a significant gain after BH correction ($m{=}16$). $\Delta$ = SICA $-$ SC (pp). Symbols: $^b$gold ICL; \textbf{bold}: $p < 0.05$; {*}\,uncorrected $p < 0.05$ (BH adj.\ $p = 0.112$); $^{3s}$\,3-seed; $^{4s}$\,4-seed confirmatory (unmarked: single-seed exploratory). Degenerate conditions ($C_0 < 5\%$: QwQ-32B AIME, Qwen2.5-14B GSM8K) yield $\Delta = 0$; oracle upper bounds are reported in Appendix~\ref{app:oracle}.}
\label{tab:main_results}
\begin{tabular}{@{}llrrrrl@{}}
\toprule
Model & Domain & $n$ & SC (\%) & SICA (\%) & $\Delta$ (pp) & $p$ \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Type C: error amplification (SC $\leq$ 40\%)}} \\
Mistral-7B & PW-D5 & 600 & 39.33 & 36.50 & $\mathbf{-2.83}$ & 0.014{*} \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Intermediate SC (SC $\sim$50--60\%, Mistral-7B only)}} \\
Mistral-7B & LogiQA & 200 & 50.00 & 51.50 & $+$1.50 & 0.581 \\
Mistral-7B & FOLIO (s123) & 204 & 54.41 & 57.35 & $+$2.94 & 0.070 \\
Mistral-7B$^{3s}$ & FOLIO & 204 & 56.53 & 56.70 & $+$0.16 & 1.000 \\
Mistral-7B & FOLIO (s456) & 204 & 55.88 & 55.88 & 0.00 & 1.000 \\
Mistral-7B & FOLIO (s789) & 204 & 59.31 & 56.86 & $-$2.45 & 0.267 \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Type A: confirmation bias (SC $\geq$ 60\%)}} \\
LLaMA-3.1-8B & FOLIO & 204 & 66.18 & 61.76 & $-$4.41 & 0.093 \\
LLaMA-3.1-8B & StrategyQA & 200 & 72.00 & 74.00 & $+$2.00 & 0.424 \\
\addlinespace
Qwen2.5-14B & FOLIO (ICL)$^b$ & 199 & 74.37 & 74.87 & $+$0.50 & 1.000 \\
Qwen2.5-14B & PW-D5 & 600 & 74.00 & 71.50 & $\mathbf{-2.50}$ & 0.011{*} \\
Qwen2.5-14B$^{4s}$ & FOLIO & 204 & 75.49 & 74.51 & $-$0.98 & 1.000 \\
Qwen2.5-7B & FOLIO & 204 & 75.98 & 76.47 & $+$0.49 & 1.000 \\
Qwen2.5-14B & LogiQA & 200 & 79.00 & 78.00 & $-$1.00 & 0.625 \\
\addlinespace
Qwen3-14B & FOLIO & 204 & 84.80 & 84.31 & $-$0.49 & 1.000 \\
Qwen3-14B & PW-D5 & 600 & 85.83 & 85.67 & $-$0.17 & 1.000 \\
Qwen3-14B (think) & FOLIO & 204 & 86.27 & 86.76 & $+$0.49 & 1.000 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table*}

\looseness=-1 No non-degenerate condition shows a significant SICA effect after FDR control (BH, $m{=}16$). Two show nominally significant degradation: Mistral-7B on ProofWriter ($-2.83$\,pp, raw $p = 0.014$) and Qwen2.5-14B on ProofWriter ($-2.50$\,pp, raw $p = 0.011$); adjusted $p = 0.112$ for both. The intermediate-SC region (50--60\%) contains the only positive trends, none reaching $p < 0.05$. An aggregate sign test across self-extraction conditions yields 5 positive and 10 negative $\Delta$ values ($p = 0.30$, two-sided); including all conditions gives 8+/15$-$ ($p = 0.21$). Three-seed replication on Mistral-7B confirms seed-level noise: two of three seeds produce null or negative $\Delta$ (mean $+0.16 \pm 2.70$\,pp; Table~\ref{tab:multi-seed}). Four-seed replication on Qwen2.5-14B $\times$ FOLIO confirms the single-seed pattern: $\Delta \in [0.00, -2.01]$\,pp (mean $-1.24 \pm 0.86$; Table~\ref{tab:multi-seed}). TOST equivalence tests \citep{lakens2017equivalence} with margin $\pm 2$\,pp confirm 4 equivalent, 2 genuinely different (both negative), 10 underpowered. For the 10 underpowered conditions, our tests cannot rule out effects smaller than 1.86--4.84\,pp at 80\% power; the largest study ($n{=}804$) achieves MDE $= 1.86$\,pp (Appendix~\ref{app:power}). Absence of evidence is not evidence of absence for small effects. Margin sensitivity is robust: at $\pm 1$\,pp, 0/16 equivalent; at $\pm 3$\,pp, 10/16 equivalent; no margin yields a significant positive effect (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:tost-sensitivity}). We adopt $\pm 2$\,pp based on the lower bound of SC literature gains (2--5\,pp \citep{wang2023sc}), acknowledging this choice is anchored to SC effect sizes. We trace the failure below.


\looseness=-1 Oracle controls replacing self-extracted constraints with gold annotations confirm the MAX-SAT mechanism is sound ($+29.90$/$+14.22$\,pp FOLIO, $+17.17$\,pp ProofWriter; $p < 0.001$), yet self-extraction captures only ${\sim}$12\% of this ceiling (Appendix~\ref{app:oracle}).

Self-Consistency (SC) majority voting over chain-of-thought traces saturates as sample count grows because same-model traces are correlated voters.
We investigate whether symbolic constraint extraction can break this plateau through Symbolic Invariant Consensus Aggregation (SICA), which extracts logical constraints from reasoning traces and selects answers via weighted partial MAX-SAT.
Across six open-source LLMs (7B--32B) on three logical reasoning domains with over 3,000 condition-evaluations (${\sim}$1,250 unique instances), we find no evidence of improvement (aggregate sign test: 5+/10$-$, $p = 0.30$; none of sixteen non-degenerate conditions shows a significant positive effect after FDR control), with equivalence established in four conditions, significant degradation in two, and ten remaining underpowered for effects below ${\sim}$2 percentage points.
We trace the failure to \emph{symbolic confirmation bias} (SCB): on incorrect problems, 83.3\% of self-extracted constraints support the wrong majority answer (bias ratios ranging from $1.66\times$ to $4.97\times$), but a shuffle control shows this bias is structural---it reflects trace-count distributions rather than extraction-specific error ($\text{BR}_\text{obs} \approx \text{BR}_\text{null}$, $p > 0.7$). MAX-SAT produces answers identical to count-only aggregation on 94.4\% of problems, confirming that the formal verification layer adds no information beyond majority voting despite 99\% of constraints passing Z3 validation.
Cross-model extraction confirms SCB universality across nine models from 7B to frontier (BR $1.66$--$4.97\times$), though frontier models use cross-model rather than self-extraction.
Twenty-seven training-free remediation strategies spanning fifteen families all fail, confirming a persistent independence-accuracy trade-off.
Oracle controls confirm the aggregation mechanism is sound ($+29.90$\,pp, $+14.22$\,pp FOLIO, $+17.17$\,pp ProofWriter; $p < 0.001$); same-model self-extraction captures only ${\sim}$12\% of this ceiling.
Cross-architecture NLI verification escapes the bottleneck ($+7.00$\,pp zero-shot on the weakest generator, $p < 0.001$; $+$13--26\,pp with domain adaptation extending to generators with SC up to 72\%), with gain decreasing monotonically with generator capability ($\rho = 1.0$, $p = 0.003$, $n{=}6$).
Three zero-cost diagnostics ($K_\text{eff}$, BR, $C_0$) correctly classify all 60 tested conditions, giving practitioners an a priori prediction of whether symbolic aggregation will help.

\section{Experiments}
\label{sec:experiments}

\subsection{Setup}
\label{sec:exp-setup}

We evaluate SICA against Self-Consistency (SC) across six models, three reasoning domains, and over 3,000 condition-evaluations (${\sim}$1,250 unique instances), with diagnostic analyses of confirmation bias and process-level independence (\S\ref{sec:analysis}).

\paragraph{Models.} Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen3-14B (non-thinking mode)~\citep{yang2024qwen25}, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3~\citep{jiang2023mistral}, LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct~\citep{dubey2024llama3}, and QwQ-32B~\citep{qwen2024qwq} (7B--32B). We additionally evaluate SCB universality via cross-model extraction on five frontier models (gpt-4o, gpt-4.1, gpt-5.5, o3, Gemini-2.5-Pro; Table~\ref{tab:frontier-scb}), where Mistral-7B extracts constraints from the target model's traces since closed-source APIs do not expose internals suitable for self-extraction.

\paragraph{Datasets.} FOLIO~\citep{han2022folio} ($n{=}204$, with gold logical annotations), ProofWriter depth-5~\citep{tafjord2021proofwriter} ($n{=}600$), LogiQA~\citep{liu2020logiqa} ($n{=}200$). StrategyQA~\citep{geva2021strategyqa} ($n{=}200$) serves as a domain-formalizability diagnostic. GSM8K~\citep{cobbe2021gsm8k} (exploratory, $n{=}30$) and AIME 2024 ($n{=}22$) probe the degenerate regime ($C_0 < 5\%$).

McNemar exact test ($\alpha{=}0.05$); 95\% bootstrap CIs ($10{,}000$ resamples) for $n \geq 200$. SICA incurs $4.5{\times}$ SC wall-clock; extraction accounts for 76\% of overhead.

Self-Consistency (SC) majority voting over chain-of-thought traces saturates as sample count grows because same-model traces are correlated voters.
We investigate whether symbolic constraint extraction can break this plateau through Symbolic Invariant Consensus Aggregation (SICA), which extracts logical constraints from reasoning traces and selects answers via weighted partial MAX-SAT.
Across six open-source LLMs (7B--32B) on three logical reasoning domains with over 3,000 condition-evaluations (${\sim}$1,250 unique instances), we find no evidence of improvement (aggregate sign test: 7+/7$-$, $p = 1.00$; none of fifteen non-degenerate conditions shows a significant positive effect after FDR control), with equivalence established in four conditions, significant degradation in two, and ten remaining underpowered for effects below ${\sim}$2 percentage points.
We trace the failure to \emph{symbolic confirmation bias} (SCB): on incorrect problems, 83.3\% of self-extracted constraints support the wrong majority answer (bias ratios ranging from $1.66\times$ to $4.97\times$), but a shuffle control shows this bias is structural---it reflects trace-count distributions rather than extraction-specific error ($\text{BR}_\text{obs} \approx \text{BR}_\text{null}$, $p > 0.7$). MAX-SAT produces answers identical to count-only aggregation on 94.4\% of problems, confirming that the formal verification layer adds no information beyond majority voting despite 99\% of constraints passing Z3 validation.
Cross-model extraction confirms SCB universality across nine models from 7B to frontier (BR $1.66$--$4.97\times$), though frontier models use cross-model rather than self-extraction.
Twenty-seven training-free remediation strategies spanning fifteen families all fail, confirming a persistent independence-accuracy trade-off.
Oracle controls confirm the aggregation mechanism is sound ($+29.90$\,pp, $+14.22$\,pp FOLIO, $+17.17$\,pp ProofWriter; $p < 0.001$); same-model self-extraction captures only ${\sim}$12\% of this ceiling.
Cross-architecture NLI verification escapes the bottleneck ($+7.00$\,pp zero-shot on the weakest generator, $p < 0.001$; $+$13--26\,pp with domain adaptation extending to generators with SC up to 72\%), with gain decreasing monotonically with generator capability ($\rho = 1.0$, $p = 0.003$, $n{=}6$).
Three zero-cost diagnostics ($K_\text{eff}$, BR, $C_0$) correctly classify all 60 tested conditions, giving practitioners an a priori prediction of whether symbolic aggregation will help.

\section{Experiments}
\label{sec:experiments}

\subsection{Setup}
\label{sec:exp-setup}

We evaluate SICA against Self-Consistency (SC) across six models, three reasoning domains, and over 3,000 condition-evaluations (${\sim}$1,250 unique instances), with diagnostic analyses of confirmation bias and process-level independence (\S\ref{sec:analysis}).

\paragraph{Models.} Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen3-14B (non-thinking mode)~\citep{yang2024qwen25}, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3~\citep{jiang2023mistral}, LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct~\citep{dubey2024llama3}, and QwQ-32B~\citep{qwen2024qwq} (7B--32B). We additionally evaluate SCB universality via cross-model extraction on five frontier models (gpt-4o, gpt-4.1, gpt-5.5, o3, Gemini-2.5-Pro; Table~\ref{tab:frontier-scb}), where Mistral-7B extracts constraints from the target model's traces since closed-source APIs do not expose internals suitable for self-extraction.

\paragraph{Datasets.} FOLIO~\citep{han2022folio} ($n{=}204$, with gold logical annotations), ProofWriter depth-5~\citep{tafjord2021proofwriter} ($n{=}600$), LogiQA~\citep{liu2020logiqa} ($n{=}200$). StrategyQA~\citep{geva2021strategyqa} ($n{=}200$) serves as a domain-formalizability diagnostic. GSM8K~\citep{cobbe2021gsm8k} (exploratory, $n{=}30$) and AIME 2024 ($n{=}22$) probe the degenerate regime ($C_0 < 5\%$).

\paragraph{Parameters.} $K{=}12$ traces at $T{=}0.7$, extraction at $T_{\text{ext}}{=}0.3$, $\alpha{=}0.5$, Z3 timeout 10s. McNemar exact test ($\alpha{=}0.05$); 95\% bootstrap CIs ($10{,}000$ resamples) for $n \geq 200$. SICA incurs $4.5{\times}$ SC wall-clock; extraction accounts for 76\% of overhead.


\subsection{Main Results}
\label{sec:main-results}

Table~\ref{tab:main_results} reports accuracy across all conditions sorted by SC baseline, revealing three observation-driven accuracy regimes.

\begin{table*}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{SICA vs.\ SC across all non-degenerate self-extraction conditions (sorted by SC). No condition shows a significant gain after BH correction ($m{=}16$). $\Delta$ = SICA $-$ SC (pp). Symbols: $^b$gold ICL; \textbf{bold}: $p < 0.05$; {*}\,uncorrected $p < 0.05$ (BH adj.\ $p = 0.112$); $^{3s}$\,3-seed; $^{4s}$\,4-seed confirmatory (unmarked: single-seed exploratory). Degenerate conditions ($C_0 < 5\%$: QwQ-32B AIME, Qwen2.5-14B GSM8K) yield $\Delta = 0$; oracle upper bounds are reported in Appendix~\ref{app:oracle}.}
\label{tab:main_results}
\begin{tabular}{@{}llrrrrl@{}}
\toprule
Model & Domain & $n$ & SC (\%) & SICA (\%) & $\Delta$ (pp) & $p$ \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Type C: error amplification (SC $\leq$ 40\%)}} \\
Mistral-7B & PW-D5 & 600 & 39.33 & 36.50 & $\mathbf{-2.83}$ & 0.014{*} \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Intermediate SC (SC $\sim$50--60\%, Mistral-7B only)}} \\
Mistral-7B & LogiQA & 200 & 50.00 & 51.50 & $+$1.50 & 0.581 \\
Mistral-7B & FOLIO (s123) & 204 & 54.41 & 57.35 & $+$2.94 & 0.070 \\
Mistral-7B$^{3s}$ & FOLIO & 204 & 56.53 & 56.70 & $+$0.16 & 1.000 \\
Mistral-7B & FOLIO (s456) & 204 & 55.88 & 55.88 & 0.00 & 1.000 \\
Mistral-7B & FOLIO (s789) & 204 & 59.31 & 56.86 & $-$2.45 & 0.267 \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Type A: confirmation bias (SC $\geq$ 60\%)}} \\
LLaMA-3.1-8B & FOLIO & 204 & 66.18 & 61.76 & $-$4.41 & 0.093 \\
LLaMA-3.1-8B & StrategyQA & 200 & 72.00 & 74.00 & $+$2.00 & 0.424 \\
\addlinespace

Qwen2.5-14B & PW-D5 & 600 & 74.00 & 71.50 & $\mathbf{-2.50}$ & 0.011{*} \\

\addlinespace
Qwen3-14B & FOLIO & 204 & 83.33 & 84.80 & $+$1.47 & 1.000 \\
Qwen3-14B & PW-D5 & 600 & 85.83 & 85.67 & $-$0.17 & 1.000 \\

\looseness=-1 No non-degenerate condition shows a significant SICA effect after FDR control (BH, $m{=}16$). Two show nominally significant degradation: Mistral-7B on ProofWriter ($-2.83$\,pp, raw $p = 0.014$) and Qwen2.5-14B on ProofWriter ($-2.50$\,pp, raw $p = 0.011$); adjusted $p = 0.112$ for both. The intermediate-SC region (50--60\%) contains the only positive trends, none reaching $p < 0.05$. An aggregate sign test across self-extraction conditions yields 7 positive and 7 negative $\Delta$ values ($p = 1.00$, two-sided). Three-seed replication on Mistral-7B confirms seed-level noise: two of three seeds produce null or negative $\Delta$ (mean $+0.16 \pm 2.70$\,pp; Table~\ref{tab:multi-seed}). Four-seed replication on Qwen2.5-14B $\times$ FOLIO confirms the single-seed pattern: $\Delta \in [0.00, -2.01]$\,pp (mean $-1.24 \pm 0.86$; Table~\ref{tab:multi-seed}). TOST equivalence tests \citep{lakens2017equivalence} with margin $\pm 2$\,pp confirm 4 equivalent, 2 genuinely different (both negative), 10 underpowered. For the 10 underpowered conditions, our tests cannot rule out effects smaller than 1.86--4.84\,pp at 80\% power; the largest study ($n{=}804$) achieves MDE $= 1.86$\,pp (Appendix~\ref{app:power}). Absence of evidence is not evidence of absence for small effects. Margin sensitivity is robust: at $\pm 1$\,pp, 0/16 equivalent; at $\pm 3$\,pp, 10/16 equivalent; no margin yields a significant positive effect (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:tost-sensitivity}). We adopt $\pm 2$\,pp based on the lower bound of SC literature gains (2--5\,pp \citep{wang2023sc}), acknowledging this choice is anchored to SC effect sizes. We trace the failure below.

content.text:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   This is a Paper Agent session for the "symb_invariant_consensus" EMNLP 2026 paper, handling sequential Director data correction patches following D061 tiebreaking correction. The session continues from prior work (Tasks A-C and the beginning of D152). The primary work involves:
   - D152: Major narrative + data patch across all paper files (solutions.tex, abstract.tex, introduction.tex, discussion.tex, appendix.tex, scatter plot)
   - Director supplementary data: Full combo table w=1/3/5 precise values + BH recalculation
   - Table 1 partial update: 3 confirmed rows (Mistral LogiQA, Qwen2.5 LogiQA, Qwen3 PW-D5)
   - Table 1 final corrections: 2 rows with swapped columns (Qwen2.5 FOLIO, Qwen3 FOLIO)
   - Sign test corrections: Two rounds of updates, final value "8+/7−, p = 1.00"

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - EMNLP 2026: 8-page strict main text limit (Limitations/References don't count)
   - Symbolic Confirmation Bias (SCB): BR 1.66×–4.97× across nine models
   - D061 tiebreaking correction: Changed SC baselines for multiple conditions
   - Benjamini-Hochberg correction: m=12 for NLI combo (2/12 survive: Mistral w=3 and w=5), m=16 for main Table 1
   - Sign test: binomtest on non-degenerate conditions excluding ties
   - McNemar exact test for pairwise comparisons
   - Cross-architecture NLI escape: DeBERTa-large-mnli (55% standalone) + DeBERTa fine-tuned (99.67%)
   - Capability gap hypothesis: combo gain decreases monotonically with generator SC
   - PID alignment difference: Table 1 uses SC=39.33% (SICA pipeline), Table 3 uses SC=39.17% (combo eval)
   - \enlargethispage{14\baselineskip} for page fitting
   - Spearman ρ=1.0, p=0.003, n=6

3. Files and Code Sections:

   - **abstract.tex** — Core paper abstract
     - Updated sign test: "5+/10−, p = 0.30" → "8+/7−, p = 1.00"
     - Updated condition count: "sixteen non-degenerate conditions" (final)
     - Current L3: `we find no evidence of improvement (aggregate sign test: 8+/7$-$, $p = 1.00$; none of sixteen non-degenerate conditions shows a significant positive effect after FDR control)`
     - L8 (from D152): `Cross-architecture NLI verification escapes the bottleneck ($+7.00$\,pp zero-shot on the weakest generator, $p < 0.001$; $+$13--26\,pp with domain adaptation extending to generators with SC up to 72\%)`

   - **experiments.tex** — §4 Main Results with Table 1
     - Table 1 updated rows (3 confirmed + 2 final):
       - L34: `Mistral-7B & LogiQA & 200 & 50.00 & 51.50 & $+$1.50 & 0.581 \\`
       - L46: `Qwen2.5-14B$^{4s}$ & FOLIO & 204 & 75.98 & 75.49 & $-$0.49 & 1.000 \\`
       - L48: `Qwen2.5-14B & LogiQA & 200 & 79.00 & 78.00 & $-$1.00 & 0.625 \\`
       - L50: `Qwen3-14B & FOLIO & 204 & 83.33 & 84.80 & $+$1.47 & 1.000 \\`
       - L51: `Qwen3-14B & PW-D5 & 600 & 85.83 & 85.67 & $-$0.17 & 1.000 \\`
     - L31 UNCHANGED: `Mistral-7B & PW-D5 & 600 & 39.33 & 36.50 & $\mathbf{-2.83}$ & 0.014{*} \\` (Director: Table 1 keeps 39.33)
     - Sign test text (L57): `An aggregate sign test across self-extraction conditions yields 8 positive and 7 negative $\Delta$ values ($p = 1.00$, two-sided).`
     - Table caption keeps m=16

   - **diagnosis.tex** — §5 Diagnosis with Table 1 duplicate and Table 2
     - Same 5 Table 1 rows updated as experiments.tex
     - L4: `None of sixteen non-degenerate conditions shows a significant positive effect`
     - Table 2 (independence table) updated:
       - L67: `Qwen2.5-14B & LogiQA & 0.82 & 1.20 & 79.00 & $-$1.00 \\`
       - L68: `Qwen3 & FOLIO & 0.77 & 1.26 & 83.33 & $+$1.47 \\`
       - L69: `Qwen2.5-14B & FOLIO & 0.74 & 1.30 & 75.98 & $-$0.49 \\`
       - L73: `Mistral-7B & LogiQA & 0.51 & 1.81 & 50.00 & $+$1.50 \\`

   - **solutions.tex** — §6 Cross-Architecture Proof-of-Concept (updated in D152, confirmed in this session)
     - Table 3 (cross_generator_nli): Mistral 39.17/+15.83/+7.00, LLaMA 72.50/-17.50/+0.83, Qwen2.5 74.00/-19.00/+0.67, Qwen3 85.83/-30.83/+0.50
     - Main result, Capability gap, Domain-adapted paragraphs all rewritten in D152

   - **appendix.tex** — Multiple tables and text updated:
     - Full combo table (tab:nli-combo-full): All 12 rows updated with Director's precise values + BH recalculated:
       - Mistral w=1: `& 1 & 40.33 & $+$1.17 & .189 & .630 & \\`
       - Mistral w=3: `& 3 & 46.17 & $+$7.00 & $5.0{\times}10^{-6}$ & $3.00{\times}10^{-5}$ & {***} \\`
       - LLaMA w=1: `& 1 & 73.33 & $+$0.83 & .359 & .720 & \\`

     - DRC table (tab:drc): SC 39.33→39.17 (other values pending)
     - Figure 7 caption: "SC ≤ 70%" → "only for generators below the verifier's standalone accuracy"; removed "~values"

     - Type B text: Mistral LogiQA SC/Δ/p and Qwen2.5 LogiQA Δ/p updated

   - **gen_capability_gap_scatter.py** — Scatter plot script updated with D152 data:
     - deberta_pts: Qwen2.5 PW (-19.00, 0.67), Mistral PW (15.83, 7.00)
     - llama_pt: (-17.50, 0.83)

     - Regenerated PDF/PNG successfully

\section{Experiments}
\label{sec:experiments}

\subsection{Setup}
\label{sec:exp-setup}

We evaluate SICA against Self-Consistency (SC) across six models, three reasoning domains, and over 3,000 condition-evaluations (${\sim}$1,250 unique instances), with diagnostic analyses of confirmation bias and process-level independence (\S\ref{sec:analysis}).

\paragraph{Models.} Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen3-14B (non-thinking mode)~\citep{yang2024qwen25}, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3~\citep{jiang2023mistral}, LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct~\citep{dubey2024llama3}, and QwQ-32B~\citep{qwen2024qwq} (7B--32B). We additionally evaluate SCB universality via cross-model extraction on five frontier models (gpt-4o, gpt-4.1, gpt-5.5, o3, Gemini-2.5-Pro; Table~\ref{tab:frontier-scb}), where Mistral-7B extracts constraints from the target model's traces since closed-source APIs do not expose internals suitable for self-extraction.

\paragraph{Datasets.} FOLIO~\citep{han2022folio} ($n{=}204$, with gold logical annotations), ProofWriter depth-5~\citep{tafjord2021proofwriter} ($n{=}600$), LogiQA~\citep{liu2020logiqa} ($n{=}200$). StrategyQA~\citep{geva2021strategyqa} ($n{=}200$) serves as a domain-formalizability diagnostic. GSM8K~\citep{cobbe2021gsm8k} (exploratory, $n{=}30$) and AIME 2024 ($n{=}22$) probe the degenerate regime ($C_0 < 5\%$).

\paragraph{Parameters.} $K{=}12$ traces at $T{=}0.7$, extraction at $T_{\text{ext}}{=}0.3$, $\alpha{=}0.5$, Z3 timeout 10s. McNemar exact test ($\alpha{=}0.05$); 95\% bootstrap CIs ($10{,}000$ resamples) for $n \geq 200$. SICA incurs $4.5{\times}$ SC wall-clock; extraction accounts for 76\% of overhead.


\subsection{Main Results}
\label{sec:main-results}

Table~\ref{tab:main_results} reports accuracy across all conditions sorted by SC baseline, revealing three observation-driven accuracy regimes.

\begin{table*}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{SICA vs.\ SC across all non-degenerate self-extraction conditions (sorted by SC). No condition shows a significant gain after BH correction ($m{=}16$). $\Delta$ = SICA $-$ SC (pp). Symbols: $^b$gold ICL; \textbf{bold}: $p < 0.05$; {*}\,uncorrected $p < 0.05$ (BH adj.\ $p = 0.112$); $^{3s}$\,3-seed; $^{4s}$\,4-seed confirmatory (unmarked: single-seed exploratory). Degenerate conditions ($C_0 < 5\%$: QwQ-32B AIME, Qwen2.5-14B GSM8K) yield $\Delta = 0$; oracle upper bounds are reported in Appendix~\ref{app:oracle}.}
\label{tab:main_results}
\begin{tabular}{@{}llrrrrl@{}}
\toprule
Model & Domain & $n$ & SC (\%) & SICA (\%) & $\Delta$ (pp) & $p$ \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Type C: error amplification (SC $\leq$ 40\%)}} \\
Mistral-7B & PW-D5 & 600 & 39.33 & 36.50 & $\mathbf{-2.83}$ & 0.014{*} \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Intermediate SC (SC $\sim$50--60\%, Mistral-7B only)}} \\
Mistral-7B & LogiQA & 200 & 50.00 & 51.50 & $+$1.50 & 0.581 \\
Mistral-7B & FOLIO (s123) & 204 & 54.41 & 57.35 & $+$2.94 & 0.070 \\
Mistral-7B$^{3s}$ & FOLIO & 204 & 56.53 & 56.70 & $+$0.16 & 1.000 \\
Mistral-7B & FOLIO (s456) & 204 & 55.88 & 55.88 & 0.00 & 1.000 \\
Mistral-7B & FOLIO (s789) & 204 & 59.31 & 56.86 & $-$2.45 & 0.267 \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Type A: confirmation bias (SC $\geq$ 60\%)}} \\
LLaMA-3.1-8B & FOLIO & 204 & 66.18 & 61.76 & $-$4.41 & 0.093 \\
LLaMA-3.1-8B & StrategyQA & 200 & 72.00 & 74.00 & $+$2.00 & 0.424 \\
\addlinespace
Qwen2.5-14B & FOLIO (ICL)$^b$ & 199 & 74.37 & 74.87 & $+$0.50 & 1.000 \\
Qwen2.5-14B & PW-D5 & 600 & 74.00 & 71.50 & $\mathbf{-2.50}$ & 0.011{*} \\
Qwen2.5-14B$^{4s}$ & FOLIO & 204 & 75.98 & 75.49 & $-$0.49 & 1.000 \\
Qwen2.5-7B & FOLIO & 204 & 75.98 & 76.47 & $+$0.49 & 1.000 \\
Qwen2.5-14B & LogiQA & 200 & 79.00 & 78.00 & $-$1.00 & 0.625 \\
\addlinespace
Qwen3-14B & FOLIO & 204 & 83.33 & 84.80 & $+$1.47 & 1.000 \\
Qwen3-14B & PW-D5 & 600 & 85.83 & 85.67 & $-$0.17 & 1.000 \\
Qwen3-14B (think) & FOLIO & 204 & 86.27 & 86.76 & $+$0.49 & 1.000 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table*}

\looseness=-1 No non-degenerate condition shows a significant SICA effect after FDR control (BH, $m{=}16$). Two show nominally significant degradation: Mistral-7B on ProofWriter ($-2.83$\,pp, raw $p = 0.014$) and Qwen2.5-14B on ProofWriter ($-2.50$\,pp, raw $p = 0.011$); adjusted $p = 0.112$ for both. The intermediate-SC region (50--60\%) contains the only positive trends, none reaching $p < 0.05$. An aggregate sign test across self-extraction conditions yields 8 positive and 7 negative $\Delta$ values ($p = 1.00$, two-sided). Three-seed replication on Mistral-7B confirms seed-level noise: two of three seeds produce null or negative $\Delta$ (mean $+0.16 \pm 2.70$\,pp; Table~\ref{tab:multi-seed}). Four-seed replication on Qwen2.5-14B $\times$ FOLIO confirms the single-seed pattern: $\Delta \in [0.00, -2.01]$\,pp (mean $-1.24 \pm 0.86$; Table~\ref{tab:multi-seed}). TOST equivalence tests \citep{lakens2017equivalence} with margin $\pm 2$\,pp confirm 4 equivalent, 2 genuinely different (both negative), 10 underpowered. For the 10 underpowered conditions, our tests cannot rule out effects smaller than 1.86--4.84\,pp at 80\% power; the largest study ($n{=}804$) achieves MDE $= 1.86$\,pp (Appendix~\ref{app:power}). Absence of evidence is not evidence of absence for small effects. Margin sensitivity is robust: at $\pm 1$\,pp, 0/16 equivalent; at $\pm 3$\,pp, 10/16 equivalent; no margin yields a significant positive effect (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:tost-sensitivity}). We adopt $\pm 2$\,pp based on the lower bound of SC literature gains (2--5\,pp \citep{wang2023sc}), acknowledging this choice is anchored to SC effect sizes. We trace the failure below.


\looseness=-1 Oracle controls replacing self-extracted constraints with gold annotations confirm the MAX-SAT mechanism is sound ($+29.90$/$+14.22$\,pp FOLIO, $+17.17$\,pp ProofWriter; $p < 0.001$), yet self-extraction captures only ${\sim}$12\% of this ceiling (Appendix~\ref{app:oracle}).

Self-Consistency (SC) majority voting over chain-of-thought traces saturates as sample count grows because same-model traces are correlated voters.
We investigate whether symbolic constraint extraction can break this plateau through Symbolic Invariant Consensus Aggregation (SICA), which extracts logical constraints from reasoning traces and selects answers via weighted partial MAX-SAT.
Across six open-source LLMs (7B--32B) on three logical reasoning domains with over 3,000 condition-evaluations (${\sim}$1,250 unique instances), we find no evidence of improvement (aggregate sign test: 8+/7$-$, $p = 1.00$; none of sixteen non-degenerate conditions shows a significant positive effect after FDR control), with equivalence established in four conditions, significant degradation in two, and ten remaining underpowered for effects below ${\sim}$2 percentage points.
We trace the failure to \emph{symbolic confirmation bias} (SCB): on incorrect problems, 83.3\% of self-extracted constraints support the wrong majority answer (bias ratios ranging from $1.66\times$ to $4.97\times$), but a shuffle control shows this bias is structural---it reflects trace-count distributions rather than extraction-specific error ($\text{BR}_\text{obs} \approx \text{BR}_\text{null}$, $p > 0.7$). MAX-SAT produces answers identical to count-only aggregation on 94.4\% of problems, confirming that the formal verification layer adds no information beyond majority voting despite 99\% of constraints passing Z3 validation.
Cross-model extraction confirms SCB universality across nine models from 7B to frontier (BR $1.66$--$4.97\times$), though frontier models use cross-model rather than self-extraction.
Twenty-seven training-free remediation strategies spanning fifteen families all fail, confirming a persistent independence-accuracy trade-off.
Oracle controls confirm the aggregation mechanism is sound ($+29.90$\,pp, $+14.22$\,pp FOLIO, $+17.17$\,pp ProofWriter; $p < 0.001$); same-model self-extraction captures only ${\sim}$12\% of this ceiling.
Cross-architecture NLI verification escapes the bottleneck ($+7.00$\,pp zero-shot on the weakest generator, $p < 0.001$; $+$13--26\,pp with domain adaptation extending to generators with SC up to 72\%), with gain decreasing monotonically with generator capability ($\rho = 1.0$, $p = 0.003$, $n{=}6$).
Three zero-cost diagnostics ($K_\text{eff}$, BR, $C_0$) correctly classify all 60 tested conditions, giving practitioners an a priori prediction of whether symbolic aggregation will help.

"""Generate capability gap scatter plot for §6.

DeBERTa-MNLI primary (6 pts) + LLaMA-8B (1 pt, distinct marker) + multi-verifier (2 pts)
+ fine-tuned DeBERTa (2 pts). All gains at w=3.
"""
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from scipy.optimize import curve_fit
from scipy.stats import spearmanr, linregress

plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.family': 'serif',
    'font.serif': ['Times New Roman', 'DejaVu Serif'],
    'font.size': 9,
    'axes.labelsize': 10,
    'axes.titlesize': 10,
    'xtick.labelsize': 8,
    'ytick.labelsize': 8,
    'legend.fontsize': 7,
    'figure.dpi': 300,
    'savefig.dpi': 300,
    'savefig.bbox': 'tight',
    'savefig.pad_inches': 0.08,
})

# Primary: DeBERTa-MNLI across model x dataset at w=3
deberta_pts = [
    (-36.76, 0.49, 'Qwen3-14B$_{\\mathrm{think}}$\n(FOLIO)'),
    (-35.29, 0.49, 'Qwen3-14B\n(FOLIO)'),
    (-30.83, 0.50, 'Qwen3-14B\n(PW-D5)'),
    (-19.00, 0.67, 'Qwen2.5-14B\n(PW-D5)'),
    (-6.37,  2.94, 'Mistral-7B\n(FOLIO)'),
    (15.83,  7.00, 'Mistral-7B\n(ProofWriter)'),
]

# LLaMA point (different model family, separate marker)
llama_pt = (-17.50, 0.83, 'LLaMA-8B\n(PW-D5)')

# Secondary: other NLI verifiers on Mistral-7B ProofWriter at w=3
multi_nli = [
    (-1.50, 4.17, 'RoBERTa'),   # 37.67 - 39.17
    (7.00,  5.17, 'BART'),       # 46.17 - 39.17
]

# Fine-tuned DeBERTa on ProofWriter OWA (99.67% standalone), w=3
finetuned_pts = [
    (27.17, 11.67, 'LLaMA-8B'),    # 99.67 - 72.50
    (60.50, 13.00, 'Mistral-7B'),   # 99.67 - 39.17
]

dx = np.array([p[0] for p in deberta_pts])
dy = np.array([p[1] for p in deberta_pts])

# DeBERTa-only (excl. LLaMA) stats
rho_excl, p_excl = spearmanr(dx, dy)
print(f"DeBERTa-only (excl LLaMA) Spearman rho={rho_excl:.3f} (n={len(dx)}, p={p_excl:.4f})")

# All DeBERTa-verifier points (incl. LLaMA)
dx_all = np.append(dx, llama_pt[0])
dy_all = np.append(dy, llama_pt[1])
rho, p_rho = spearmanr(dx_all, dy_all)
print(f"DeBERTa-all (incl LLaMA) Spearman rho={rho:.3f} (n={len(dx_all)}, p={p_rho:.4f})")
slope, intercept, r_value, p_lin, _ = linregress(dx_all, dy_all)
print(f"DeBERTa-all linear: R²={r_value**2:.3f}, p={p_lin:.4f}")

# Sigmoid with Director's parameters as guide
def sigmoid(x, L, k, x0, b):
    return L / (1 + np.exp(-k * (x - x0))) + b

# Use all points for visual fit (DeBERTa + LLaMA + multi-NLI)
all_pts = deberta_pts + [llama_pt] + multi_nli
ax_all = np.array([p[0] for p in all_pts])
ay_all = np.array([p[1] for p in all_pts])

try:
    popt, _ = curve_fit(sigmoid, ax_all, ay_all,
                        p0=[3.5, 0.3, 1.0, 0.2],
                        bounds=([0.5, 0.01, -10, -1], [5.0, 2.0, 15, 2.0]),
                        maxfev=50000)
    x_fit = np.linspace(-42, 68, 500)
    y_sig = sigmoid(x_fit, *popt)
    ss_res = np.sum((ay_all - sigmoid(ax_all, *popt))**2)
    ss_tot = np.sum((ay_all - np.mean(ay_all))**2)
    r2_sig = 1 - ss_res / ss_tot
    inflection = popt[2]
    print(f"Sigmoid ({len(ax_all)}pt): R²={r2_sig:.3f}, inflection={inflection:.1f}pp, L={popt[0]:.2f}, k={popt[1]:.3f}")
    has_sigmoid = True
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Sigmoid fit failed: {e}")
    has_sigmoid = False
    x_fit = np.linspace(-42, 68, 500)

# Plot
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(3.8, 2.8))
fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.16, bottom=0.20, right=0.96, top=0.94)

# DeBERTa primary points (Mistral/Qwen generators)
ax.scatter(dx, dy, marker='o', c='#2166ac', s=50, zorder=5,
           label='DeBERTa-MNLI', edgecolors='white', linewidths=0.5)

# LLaMA generator (different model family)
ax.scatter([llama_pt[0]], [llama_pt[1]], marker='D', c='#e66101', s=50, zorder=5,
           label='DeBERTa-MNLI (LLaMA)', edgecolors='white', linewidths=0.5)

# Multi-NLI secondary points
mx = [p[0] for p in multi_nli]
my = [p[1] for p in multi_nli]
ml = [p[2] for p in multi_nli]
ax.scatter([mx[0]], [my[0]], marker='s', c='#b2182b', s=40, zorder=5,
           label='RoBERTa-MNLI', edgecolors='white', linewidths=0.5)
ax.scatter([mx[1]], [my[1]], marker='^', c='#4dac26', s=40, zorder=5,
           label='BART-MNLI', edgecolors='white', linewidths=0.5)

# Fine-tuned DeBERTa points
fx = [p[0] for p in finetuned_pts]
fy = [p[1] for p in finetuned_pts]
ax.scatter(fx, fy, marker='*', c='#7b3294', s=100, zorder=6,
           label='Fine-tuned DeBERTa', edgecolors='white', linewidths=0.5)

# Sigmoid curve
if has_sigmoid:
    ax.plot(x_fit, y_sig, '-', color='#555555', linewidth=1.0, alpha=0.6,
            label=f'Sigmoid fit')

# Annotations for DeBERTa points
annot_config = [
    (-36.76, 0.49, 'Qwen3-14B$_{\\mathrm{think}}$\nFOLIO', (6, -3), 'left'),
    (-35.29, 0.49, 'Qwen3-14B\nFOLIO', (6, -15), 'left'),
    (-30.83, 0.50, 'Qwen3-14B\nPW-D5', (6, 3), 'left'),
    (-19.00, 0.67, 'Qwen2.5-14B\nPW-D5', (6, -8), 'left'),
    (-6.37,  2.94, 'Mistral-7B\nFOLIO', (6, -8), 'left'),
    (15.83,  7.00, 'Mistral-7B\nPW-D5', (-6, 5), 'right'),
]
for x, y, lbl, offset, ha in annot_config:
    ax.annotate(lbl, (x, y), textcoords='offset points',
                xytext=offset, fontsize=5.5, ha=ha, color='#444444',
                linespacing=0.9)

# LLaMA annotation (distinct color)
ax.annotate('LLaMA-8B\nPW-D5', (llama_pt[0], llama_pt[1]),
            textcoords='offset points', xytext=(6, -10), fontsize=5.5,
            ha='left', color='#e66101', linespacing=0.9)

# Annotations for multi-NLI
ax.annotate('RoBERTa', (mx[0], my[0]), textcoords='offset points',
            xytext=(5, 5), fontsize=5.5, ha='left', color='#b2182b')
ax.annotate('BART', (mx[1], my[1]), textcoords='offset points',
            xytext=(5, 5), fontsize=5.5, ha='left', color='#4dac26')

# Annotations for fine-tuned
ax.annotate('LLaMA-8B\n(fine-tuned)', (fx[0], fy[0]), textcoords='offset points',
            xytext=(-6, 5), fontsize=5.5, ha='right', color='#7b3294', linespacing=0.9)
ax.annotate('Mistral-7B\n(fine-tuned)', (fx[1], fy[1]), textcoords='offset points',
            xytext=(-6, 5), fontsize=5.5, ha='right', color='#7b3294', linespacing=0.9)

# Reference lines
ax.axhline(0, color='black', linewidth=0.3, alpha=0.2)
ax.axvline(0, color='black', linewidth=0.5, alpha=0.25, linestyle=':')

# Region labels
ax.text(-21, 14.0, 'verifier $<$ generator', fontsize=6.5, color='#aaaaaa',
        ha='center', style='italic')
ax.text(40, 14.0, 'verifier $>$ generator', fontsize=6.5, color='#aaaaaa',
        ha='center', style='italic')

ax.set_xlabel('Capability gap (verifier $-$ generator SC, pp)')
ax.set_ylabel('Combo gain over SC (pp, $w{=}3$)')
ax.set_xlim(-42, 68)
ax.set_ylim(-0.3, 15.0)
ax.legend(loc='lower right', framealpha=0.9, edgecolor='#cccccc',
          borderpad=0.3, handletextpad=0.4, bbox_to_anchor=(1.0, 0.0))
ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)

# no tight_layout — manual subplots_adjust above
outdir = '/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0513_3/projects/symb_invariant_consensus/docs/paper/figures'
fig.savefig(f'{outdir}/capability_gap_scatter.pdf')
fig.savefig(f'{outdir}/capability_gap_scatter.png')
print("Saved to", outdir)

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). [Director 指令] **战略写作重构任务 — 目标 4.0+**

当前状态：Round 14 评分 3.5（Borderline Conference），审稿人明确指出升分路径是 presentation 改进而非新实验。距 DDL 5/25 还有 2 天。

## 核心问题

论文实验覆盖度和统计严谨性已达顶会水准（Soundness 4/5），但 Significance（2.5-3.5/5）和 Presentation 拖了后腿。需要从整体上重新思考写作策略，而非局部修补。

## 审稿人识别的关键问题

1. **信息密度过高**：8 页正文 13 个技术缩写，审稿人认知负担大
2. **深浅不均**：§3.1 CJT 推导（非原创）占半页，§5.5 Remediation（27 种修复）只有 ~15 行，§7 Discussion 只有 1/3 页
3. **Pages 3-5 纯文字墙**：Figure 1 在 p2，Table 1 在 p6，中间 3 页无 display item
4. **Symbolic Mirage Hypothesis 措辞**：Predictions 1-2 是事后总结，只有 Prediction 3 是真正的 prediction。需要重定位为 observations + testable prediction
5. **Cross-architecture escape 结论过强**：只有 Mistral-7B 显著，需软化为 preliminary evidence
6. **Abstract power caveat 不足**：10/16 条件 underpowered
7. **惊喜度不够**：核心发现在 Huang et al. 之后可预见性高。需要突出 Z3 formal solver 场景的特殊性 — "即使加了外部求解器，extraction 偏差仍使验证层失效"

## 你的任务

**从整体反思**论文的写作策略，给出一个完整的重构方案。不要局部修补，要考虑：

1. **8 页空间的最优分配**：什么该留在正文？什么该移到附录？哪些内容值得深入展开？
2. **叙事重心**：当前论文试图在 8 页展示所有东西，结果每个都"点到即止"。选 3-4 个最强贡献深入展开，其余精简或移附录。
3. **惊喜度提升**：如何让 framing 更有冲击力？"Z3 formal solver 也被 extraction bias 击败"比"又一个 self-correction 失败"更有新闻价值。
4. **可视化策略**：Pages 3-5 的文字墙如何打破？是否需要新的 figure/table？
5. **术语瘦身**：13 个缩写哪些是必须的？哪些可以用自然语言替代？
6. **Mirage Hypothesis 重构**：怎么把 observations 和 predictions 分开，让框架更有预测力？
7. **Discussion 扩展**：三个零成本诊断 60/60 分类是很强的实用贡献，如何充分展开让审稿人 get 到价值？

**如果你的方案需要补充实验或分析**（比如新的 figure 数据、新的统计量、新的 baseline 对比），直接在方案中列出，我会让 Agent 全力支持。

请先输出 writing_plan.yaml 提交给我审批，再执行。投稿目标：EMNLP 2026 ARR May 25。引用需要验证。

47	\subsection{Symbolic Confirmation Bias}
48	\label{sec:confirmation-bias}
49	\label{sec:effective-k}
50	
51	Table~\ref{tab:independence} reports Fleiss' $\kappa$ and Effective-K (Eq.~\ref{eq:effk}) across 15 conditions at $K = 12$. Among instruction-tuned models, $\kappa$ ranges from 0.21 to 0.82, yielding $K_{\text{eff}} = 1.20\text{--}3.62$. Two conditions are jointly necessary for any positive trend: sufficient $K_{\text{eff}}$ ($\leq 1.30$ never improves) and sufficient SC accuracy ($K_{\text{eff}} = 3.62$ with SC $= 39\%$ produces significant degradation). Cross-model validation confirms universality: all four families produce $\kappa \geq 0.41$ (Table~\ref{tab:kappa_generalization}).
52	
53	This correlation manifests through a specific mechanism: self-extracted constraints systematically confirm the model's majority answer regardless of correctness. On Mistral-7B FOLIO ($n = 204$), when SICA errs, 83.3\% of extracted constraints support the incorrect majority answer---a bias ratio of $4.97\times$ compared to correct problems. Consequently, 94\% of SICA errors overlap with SC errors: symbolic aggregation adds no independent corrective signal.
54	
55	The causal chain is: the model generates an answer, then extracts logical constraints consistent with it. Constraints from majority-answer traces use trace-specific variable names (56.4\% of cross-answer pairs share zero Z3 variables), so MAX-SAT retains nearly all, and aggregation reduces to a weighted majority vote (Eq.~\ref{eq:degenerate}). Confirmation bias generalizes across model families: bias ratios of $4.97\times$ (Mistral-7B), $3.85\times$ (Qwen2.5-14B), and $2.88{\times}^{\dag}$ (LLaMA-3.1-8B) all significantly exceed $1.0$ ($^{\dag}$based on 4/12 traces due to extraction failures; Table~\ref{tab:cross-model-bias}). The oracle ceiling (\S\ref{sec:oracle}) confirms that 75.9\% of the potential gain is lost to self-extraction quality.
56	
57	\begin{table}[t]
58	\centering
59	\small
60	\caption{Trace independence metrics ($K = 12$, sorted by $\kappa$ descending). $\kappa$: Fleiss' Kappa. $K_{\text{eff}}$: Effective-K (Eq.~\ref{eq:effk}). SC: Self-Consistency baseline. $\Delta$: SICA $-$ SC (pp). {*}\,$p < 0.05$; positive $\Delta$ values do not reach significance. multi-T $= T \in \{0.3, 0.7, 1.2\}$, 4 traces each.}
61	\label{tab:independence}

63	\toprule
64	Model & Condition & $\kappa$ & $K_{\text{eff}}$ & SC (\%) & $\Delta$ (pp) \\
65	\midrule

87	\subsection{Process-Level Independence}
88	\label{sec:process-kappa}
89	
90	Answer-level $\kappa$ may underestimate the independence limitation: two traces can follow nearly identical reasoning yet reach different final answers. We define process similarity as the mean pairwise cosine similarity of TF-IDF trace representations:
91	\begin{equation}
92	\label{eq:process-sim}
93	\text{ProcessSim}(q) = \frac{2}{K(K{-}1)} \sum_{i < j} \cos(\mathbf{v}_i^q, \mathbf{v}_j^q),
94	\end{equation}
95	where $\mathbf{v}_i^q$ is the TF-IDF vector of trace $t_i$ for question $q$. On Mistral-7B FOLIO ($n = 204$), mean ProcessSim is $0.69$, far exceeding answer-level $\kappa = 0.41$. These measures are uncorrelated ($r = -0.06$, $p = 0.36$): problems with diverse answers do not exhibit diverse reasoning (Figure~\ref{fig:process-kappa}). This gap implies that interventions targeting answer diversity (temperature scaling, diverse prompting) may spread answers without altering reasoning paths.
96	
97	\begin{figure}[t]
98	\centering
99	\includegraphics[width=0.85\columnwidth]{figures/fig3_process_kappa_scatter.pdf}
100	\vspace{-2mm}
101	\caption{Answer agreement vs.\ CoT cosine similarity (Mistral-7B, FOLIO, $n{=}204$). Flat regression ($r = -0.06$, $p = 0.36$): process and answer independence are uncorrelated.}
102	\label{fig:process-kappa}
103	\end{figure}
104	
105	
106	\subsection{Regime-Dependent Effects}
107	\label{sec:main-results}
108	\label{sec:diagnostics}
109	
110	SICA effectiveness depends sharply on the accuracy regime (Figure~\ref{fig:regime-scatter}).
111	
112	\paragraph{Intermediate-SC region.} Mistral-7B on FOLIO (SC $\sim$50--60\%) shows positive directional trends in 2 of 4 seeds: $\Delta = +3.43$\,pp ($p = 0.092$) and $+2.94$\,pp ($p = 0.070$); the remaining seeds show null or negative results. No seed reaches $p < 0.05$; the 4-seed mean is $+1.47$\,pp. The default-seed and seed-456 runs share identical SC baselines (55.88\%) yet diverge ($+3.43$ vs.\ $0.00$\,pp), suggesting that seed-level constraint quality, not SC level alone, influences the effect.
113	
114	\paragraph{Type A (SC $\geq$ 60\%).} All nine Type~A conditions produce no significant positive effects. Even in-context learning with gold logical examples yields $\Delta = +0.50$\,pp (n.s.). Qwen2.5-14B on ProofWriter shows significant degradation ($\Delta = -2.50$\,pp, $p = 0.011$).
115	
116	\paragraph{Type C (SC $\leq$ 40\%).} Mistral-7B on ProofWriter ($n = 600$, SC $= 39.33\%$) shows $\Delta = -2.83$\,pp ($p = 0.014$): SICA \emph{significantly hurts} by formalizing incorrect reasoning. When $C_0 < 5\%$, nearly all traces agree and SICA reduces to SC by construction.
117	
118	Four supporting analyses confirm the mechanism: constraint ablation shows MAX-SAT and count-only agree on 94.4\% of predictions ($n = 804$); 91.8\% of constraints are discriminative but mirror the majority; effects concentrate in high-entropy problems ($+12.8$\,pp) with direction determined by accuracy regime; and hyperparameter peaks coincide with low SC baselines (Appendices~\ref{app:extraction}--\ref{app:entropy}).
119	
120	\begin{figure}[t]
121	\centering
122	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{f2_regime_scatter}
123	\caption{SICA $\Delta$ (pp) vs.\ SC baseline. Filled: $n \geq 100$; open: $n < 100$. The intermediate-SC region (50--60\%, shaded) contains the only positive trends (none reaching $p < 0.05$). Type~C: significant degradation ($p = 0.014$).}
124	\label{fig:regime-scatter}
125	\end{figure}
126	
127	
128	\subsection{Remediation: 25+ Strategies Fail}
129	\label{sec:remediation}
130	\label{sec:interventions}
131	
132	We test more than twenty remediation strategies spanning prompt engineering, method-level redesign, and ten additional directions. All produce neutral or negative results.
133	
134	\paragraph{Prompt-level interventions.} Nine strategies spanning six dimensions (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:remediation}) all fail. Contrastive prompting reduces non-discriminative constraints from 8.2\% to 6.0\%, but newly discriminative constraints still mirror the majority ($\Delta = -1.1$\,pp). Cross-model extraction fails in both directions: weaker models yield 0\% discriminative constraints; stronger models produce accuracy within $\pm 1$\,pp of self-extraction. Multi-temperature sampling ($T \in \{0.3, 0.7, 1.2\}$) yields $\Delta = 0.00$\,pp.
135	
136	\paragraph{Method-level interventions.} ICG ($\Delta \approx 0$, $p = .206$), Contrastive ($\Delta = -9.31$\,pp, $p < 0.01$), and Debate ($\Delta = -18.63$/$-23.00$\,pp, $p < 0.001$) all fail (Table~\ref{tab:method_interventions}, Appendix~\ref{app:remediation}). Ten further experiments (code verification, iterative refinement, logprob filtering, cross-model ensembles) produce neutral-to-negative results (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:additional_interventions}).
137	
138	\paragraph{Independence-accuracy trade-off.} Table~\ref{tab:kappa_generalization} compares Fleiss' $\kappa$ across four aggregation methods and three model families (Figure~\ref{fig:kappa-accuracy}). SC ($\kappa = 0.44$), Diverse-Prompt ($\kappa = 0.40$), and ICG ($\kappa = 0.47$) cluster at $\kappa \approx 0.40$--$0.47$; Debate reaches $\kappa = 0.15$ but collapses accuracy by $-18.6$\,pp. All three families cluster above $\kappa = 0.40$, forming a same-model trade-off ceiling: methods that increase independence destroy accuracy, and methods preserving accuracy cannot break the correlation floor. The bias ratio gradient ($4.97\times$ Mistral $> 3.85\times$ Qwen $> 2.88\times$ LLaMA) suggests weaker models suffer more severe confirmation bias; all models exceed $1.0$, a pattern that persists from 7B open-source to frontier closed-source (BR $1.66$--$4.97\times$; Table~\ref{tab:frontier-scb}). For practitioners, $C_0$ combined with SC accuracy predicts when augmentation is unlikely to help: $C_0 < 5\%$ implies degeneration, SC $\geq 60\%$ implies confirmation bias, SC $\leq 40\%$ implies error amplification. 1	\section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}
2	
3	Test-time computation scaling through multiple reasoning samples has emerged as a practical alternative to scaling model parameters \citep{snell2025scaling, guo2025deepseekr1}.
4	The dominant aggregation strategy, Self-Consistency (SC) \citep{wang2023sc}, samples $K$ chain-of-thought traces and selects the majority answer.
5	SC is simple, model-agnostic, and effective---but it is hitting a ceiling.
6	\citet{loo2025reevaluating} demonstrate that gains from increasing $K$ plateau and even decline for strong models.
7	The gap between SC's theoretical promise (independent correct voters converge to truth) and its practical behavior (saturating gains) points to a structural mismatch: same-model traces carry correlated errors, and majority voting has no mechanism to correct shared bias.
8	
9	Confidence-weighted \citep{taubenfeld2025cisc} and universal \citep{chen2024usc} extensions alleviate this, but the core limitation persists.
10	Recent neuro-symbolic methods \citep{pan2023logiclm, olausson2023linc, xu2026dylos, li2025aristotle, wang2025fover, luo2025logicagent} report gains on logical reasoning but introduce components beyond the reasoning model.
11	A simpler question precedes these: can the \emph{same} model extract useful formal constraints from its own traces---a zero-cost upgrade requiring no additional model or data?
12	No prior work has systematically evaluated this.
13	
14	We ground our analysis in the Condorcet Jury Theorem (CJT) \citep{condorcet1785}: if $K$ independent voters each answer correctly with probability $p > 0.5$, the majority converges to truth \citep{austensmith1996}.
15	When independence fails \citep{ladha1992correlated}, additional samples carry diminishing information.
16	Measuring inter-trace agreement with Fleiss' $\kappa$ \citep{fleiss1971kappa}, we find $\kappa = 0.21$--$0.82$ across instruction-tuned conditions, yielding $K_{\text{eff}}$ as an ordinal diagnostic of vote diversity ($K_{\text{eff}} \approx 1.2$--$3.6$ for nominal $K = 12$; \S\ref{sec:condorcet}).
17	Chain-of-thought cosine similarity ($0.69$) far exceeds answer-level $\kappa$ ($0.46$), revealing that traces share reasoning processes even when they diverge on final answers (\S\ref{sec:process-kappa}).
18	When the same model extracts logical constraints from these correlated traces, the constraints exhibit \emph{symbolic confirmation bias} (SCB): on problems where the model errs, 83.3\% of self-extracted constraints support the wrong majority answer (bias ratios $1.66$--$4.97\times$ across nine models), and 94\% of errors overlap with SC (\S\ref{sec:confirmation-bias}).
19	A shuffle control shows this bias is structural: it reflects the trace-count distribution rather than extraction-specific error.
20	Self-extraction cannot supply the independent signal that CJT requires.
21	
22	We study this through Symbolic Invariant Consensus Aggregation (SICA), which extracts logical constraints from reasoning traces and selects answers via weighted partial MAX-SAT (\S\ref{sec:pipeline}; Figure~\ref{fig:pipeline}).
23	Across six open-source models (7B--32B), three domains (FOLIO \citep{han2022folio}, ProofWriter \citep{tafjord2021proofwriter}, LogiQA \citep{liu2020logiqa}), and over 3,000 condition-evaluations with four-seed replication, twenty-seven training-free remediation strategies spanning fifteen families all produce neutral or negative results (Table~\ref{tab:main_results}).
24	Prior work shows LLMs struggle with natural-language self-correction \citep{huang2024selfcorrect} and that LLM-generated logical formulas can be unreliable \citep{stechly2025selfverification}. Our formal channel is provably sound---the failure is precisely localizable to the extraction step. The assumption that formalizing reasoning provides \emph{independent} verification evidence fails not because Z3 is unreliable (99\% of constraints are syntactically valid), but because extraction inherits the model's biases: MAX-SAT produces answers identical to count-only aggregation on 94.4\% of problems, rendering the formal layer vacuous.
25	
26	Oracle controls confirm the mechanism is sound ($+29.90$\,pp Mistral-7B, $+13.73$\,pp Qwen-14B on FOLIO, $p < 0.001$; Appendix~\ref{app:oracle}), yet self-extraction captures only ${\sim}$12\% of this ceiling.
27	The central finding is a persistent independence-accuracy trade-off \citep{krogh1994neural}: Debate reduces $\kappa$ to 0.15 but collapses accuracy ($-18.6$\,pp); other methods cluster at $\kappa \approx 0.40$--$0.47$, a same-model ceiling across three families (\S\ref{sec:remediation}).
28	A cross-architecture proof-of-concept escapes the bottleneck: zero-shot DeBERTa NLI yields $+6.67$\,pp on Mistral-7B ProofWriter ($p < 0.001$) but no significant gain for stronger generators; domain-adapted NLI amplifies gains to $+$12--26\,pp ($p < 0.0001$), extending to generators with SC up to 72\% (\S\ref{sec:cross-arch}).
29	
30	Our contributions are:
31	\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
32	\item \textbf{Quantifying symbolic confirmation bias in formal self-verification.} While the general difficulty of LLM self-correction is known \citep{huang2024selfcorrect}, we provide the first quantitative characterization of symbolic confirmation bias in formal self-verification, demonstrating that provably sound verification machinery becomes informationally vacuous under self-extraction: 83.3\% of self-extracted constraints support the wrong answer (BR $1.66$--$4.97\times$ across nine models), yet 99\% pass Z3 validation. A shuffle control and MAX-SAT ablation show this bias is structural---the formal layer adds no information beyond majority voting. Twenty-seven training-free strategies fail to break it; cross-model extraction confirms universality across nine models from 7B to frontier (\S\ref{sec:confirmation-bias}).
33	
34	\item \textbf{General diagnostic framework for trace-aggregation methods.} Three diagnostics ($K_\text{eff}$, BR, $C_0$) correctly predict success or failure across all 60 tested conditions spanning self-extraction, training-free remediation, cross-architecture verification, and oracle controls. Decision boundaries---$C_0 < 5\%$ (degenerate), $K_\text{eff} \leq 1.3$ (diversity-limited), $\text{BR} > 2\times$ (bias-dominated), $\kappa_\text{same} \geq 0.40$ (same-model ceiling)---provide zero-cost prediction of symbolic aggregation viability. The framework extends to any method extracting structured representations from LLM traces (\S\ref{sec:remediation}, \S\ref{sec:cross-arch}).
35	
36	\item \textbf{Process-level independence analysis.} CoT cosine similarity ($0.69$--$0.79$) exceeds answer-level $\kappa$ ($0.45$--$0.74$) across four models from three families; under cross-model extraction on frontier models, SICA gain decreases monotonically with process similarity ($\rho = -1.0$, $p = 0.008$; \S\ref{sec:process-kappa}).
37	\end{enumerate}

\label{fig:regime-scatter}

\section{Prompt Templates}
\label{app:prompts}

SICA uses domain-specific prompt templates for constraint extraction: one for mathematical reasoning (GSM8K, AIME) and one for logical reasoning (ProofWriter, FOLIO). Both share the same system prompt. The LLM is called with temperature $T{=}0.3$, max tokens $1024$, and structured JSON output mode. Up to 6 traces are processed in parallel via thread pooling, with 2 retries on failure (exponential backoff, base 0.5s).

\paragraph{System Prompt.}

\begin{lstlisting}
You are a constraint extraction tool. Output ONLY
valid JSON. Do NOT solve problems, reason about
correctness, or think step-by-step. Extract
constraints from the given trace exactly as stated.
\end{lstlisting}

\paragraph{Mathematical Constraint Extraction (EXTRACTION\_PROMPT).}

Used for GSM8K and AIME datasets. The placeholder \texttt{\{trace\}} is replaced with the reasoning trace at runtime.

\begin{lstlisting}
Extract mathematical constraints from this reasoning
trace as a JSON object.

Rules:
- type: "equation", "inequality", or "predicate"
- expression: human-readable, e.g. "x + y == 14"
- z3_formula: a single comparison expression in
  Python Z3 syntax
- source_step: step number where the constraint
  appears
- Use variable names from the trace

z3_formula MUST follow these rules:
- Allowed operators: ==, !=, <, >, <=, >=, +, -, *,
  /, **, %
- Use individual named variables: a1, a2, a3...
  NOT arrays a[1] or sets A
- Expand all sums explicitly:
  "a1 + a2 + a3 == 55" NOT "sum([a1,a2,a3])"
- NO Python builtins: sum(), len(), max(), min(),
  list(), set(), range(), int()
- Each z3_formula must be exactly ONE comparison
  (==, !=, <, >, <=, >=)
- For multiple values, write separate constraints
  for each

Output ONLY the JSON below, nothing else:
{"constraints": [{"type": "equation",
  "expression": "x + y == 14",
  "z3_formula": "x + y == 14",
  "source_step": 1}],
 "answer": "final_answer",
 "variables": ["x", "y"]}

Trace:
{trace}
\end{lstlisting}

\paragraph{Logical Constraint Extraction (LOGIC\_EXTRACTION\_PROMPT).}

Used for ProofWriter and FOLIO datasets.

\begin{lstlisting}
IMPORTANT: You are an EXTRACTION tool, NOT a problem
solver.
